name: card-deck
title: Card deck
description: A standard 52-card deck, optionally several decks and jokers: create, shuffle through an injected random source, deal, burn, and read card codes on server, web, Apple and Android.

facilities.description: Create, shuffle, deal and burn cards; card codes, colours and names

text.purpose: Every card game needs the same data: which cards exist, how to name them, how to shuffle them fairly, and how to hand them out. This component holds that and nothing about any particular game. A card is a two-character code (rank 2-9, T, J, Q, K, A, then suit c, d, h, s; jokers are `*r` and `*b`). A `Deck` is an immutable pair of piles: cards still to deal and cards burned. `shuffleDeck` shuffles through an injected random source, so tests can replay a deal. Clients get the data side of cards (colour, suit glyph, court name, rank label) without any drawing code; faces belong to `card-graphics`.
text.userInputs: The installer collects two settings. `decks` is how many 52-card packs to combine (whole number, 1 to 8; default 1). `jokers` adds two jokers per pack when true (default false).
text.integration: Server code builds a deck from the settings, shuffles it with the `random-source` the recipe connects, and deals with `deal(deck, n)`. Cards come off the end of the pile, first card first. Rules components (`holdem-rules`, `poker-hand-ranking`, `poker-odds`) use `parseCard`, `rankOf` and `suitOf`. Client code uses `cardFacts` (web) or `CardCode` (Apple, Android) to decide colour, glyph and court name before handing the result to a graphics component. The required `random-source` is used through one method, `shuffle(items)`; a created fair-shuffle source (`createSource`, `seededSource`, `secureSource`, `sourceFrom`) has it, and so does any object with that method, so the component is testable without the shuffle component. `cardCodes` is the `CardCodes` object (ranks, suits, names, `rankOf`, `suitOf`, `fullDeck`) that poker-hand-ranking takes.
text.infrastructure: No deployed service and no accounts; local library functions only.
text.verification: `tests/web.test.ts` (required-local) checks the 52-card pack, jokers and decks counts, code parsing against `tests/fixtures/cards.json`, shuffling through an injected source, `cardCodes`, deal order and errors, burn, and a nine-player hold'em deal. `tests/native.py apple` compiles `CardCode.swift` with swiftc and checks the same fixture (run and passed on this machine). `tests/native.py android` compiles `CardCode.kt` with kotlinc and checks the same fixture; kotlinc is not installed here, so it was written but not run. `authoring/integration.test.ts` (not packaged) deals with the real fair-shuffle sibling and ranks with the real poker-hand-ranking sibling.
text.scenarios: A hold'em table shuffles a single deck each hand. A game with several decks (a shoe) sets `decks` to 6. A rummy-style game sets `jokers` to true. A test fixes the deal by injecting a source that reorders the deck in a known way.
text.updates: Patch updates replace the files only. Card codes and the order of `createDeck` are part of the contract: changing either is a new major version. The component keeps no data.

agentInstructions: Select this component for any game that deals playing cards. Set `decks` and `jokers` from the recipe's answers (hold'em: 1 deck, no jokers). Connect a `random-source` (fair-shuffle) to its required `random-source` port. Include the web, Apple and Android client files only when the matching client targets are selected.
developerInstructions: Call `createShuffledDeck(settings, source)` once per round and keep the returned `Deck` in game state; every operation returns a new deck. Do not draw card faces here; use `card-graphics`. If your game has extra card values, add them in your own rules component, not in the code table here.

suitability.notes: Pure library; no provider limits apply.
